source: Refreshed by daily scheduled task on 2026-05-07. Loved-list cross-check ran across all 14 Loved titles — no new sequel/continuation dropped between May 6 and May 7. Confirmed unchanged: Foundation S4 → Summer/Fall 2027 (filming wraps May 2026 in Prague); Severance S3 → June or Sept 2027 (filming Apr–Dec 2026, four-season plan locked); Slow Horses S6 → ~Sep 15, 2026 (filmed and in post); Good Omens 90-min finale → May 13, 2026 (3:01am ET); Black Mirror S8 → late 2027/early 2028 (still in writing); Rick and Morty S9 → Adult Swim May 24, US streaming Aug 31; Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle Part 2 → 2027 at earliest, Part 3 → 2029 (Ufotable confirmed Part 2 NOT in 2026 lineup). Solar Opposites: confirmed ended with S6 (Oct 2025), no new continuation. HERO ROTATION: Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle exits at Day 28 of the 4-week window (Apr 9 + 28 = May 7); rotated to Tier 3 hero. Watchlist availability check ran across all 5 titles — Kevin, The Boys S5, Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle, Widow's Bay, Your Friends & Neighbors S2 — all already streamable; no new flips today. New today: Devil May Cry S2 confirmed for Netflix May 12, 2026 — Studio Mir adult-animation action with supernatural/Dante-Vergil arc; added to new_this_week and upcoming_alerts. Ladies First (Netflix May 22 Sacha Baron Cohen / Rosamund Pike gender-swap satire) added as a 'try' pick. Lord of the Flies critic score now confirmed at 92% RT Certified Fresh (audience 57% — flagged in why-line).

hero.title: Widow's Bay
hero.date: Apr 28 — airing weekly (Ep 3 drops Wed May 7, today)
hero.about: Matthew Rhys-led comedy-horror from creator Katie Dippold (The Heat, Ghostbusters 2016). 100% RT (34 reviews) on debut. Small coastal town, supernatural undercurrents, off-beat tone with an ensemble cast. Currently in weekly rollout — Ep 3 lands Wed May 7.
hero.why: Tier 3 hero pick — top critic-validated drop on a service you have, AND on your watchlist. 100% RT + off-beat horror-comedy + supernatural + ensemble + Katie Dippold (creator of The Heat, which you Loved) quadruple-stacks your reward signals. Three eps available today means a clean weekend catch-up before the next episode.

new_this_week.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — Infinity Castle
new_this_week.date: Apr 9 — now streaming (last day in 4-week window)
new_this_week.about: First film in the trilogy adapting the Infinity Castle arc — climactic showdown between the Demon Slayer Corps and Muzan's Upper Moons inside the shape-shifting fortress. Picks up directly from Hashira Training Arc. Ufotable animation. Made nearly $700M theatrically. Part 2 confirmed for 2027 at earliest, Part 3 for 2029.
new_this_week.why: Loved-list franchise + on your watchlist + actually streaming — last day inside the 4-week window before it rotates out of recommendations. If you haven't watched it yet, this is the week.

new_this_week.title: Lord of the Flies
new_this_week.date: May 4 — now streaming, all 4 eps available
new_this_week.about: Four-episode BBC/Netflix miniseries from Emmy-winner Jack Thorne (Adolescence, His Dark Materials), adapting William Golding's novel — schoolboys stranded on an island, society breaks down. Marc Munden directs. The Hollywood Reporter calls it 'very close to a definitive adaptation.'
new_this_week.why: Book adaptation is a positive signal for you; psychological pressure-cooker setup has plot-twist potential. 92% RT but audience score is mixed (57%) — critics rewarded the prestige craft, audience found it bleak. Tonally darker than your usual sweet spot — try the first ep before committing to all four.

new_this_week.title: BEEF S2
new_this_week.about: Lee Sung Jin's Emmy-sweeping anthology resets with new cast and story: Oscar Isaac, Carey Mulligan, Charles Melton, Cailee Spaeny. Two couples at a Montecito beach club — the younger pair blackmails the older pair after catching them on video in a violent fight. Eight ~30-min episodes binge-dropped. 86% RT.
new_this_week.why: S1 was praised for exactly the things you reward — dark humor, plot escalation, ensemble acting — and the anthology reset means no S1 baggage.

new_this_week.title: La Brea S1–4
new_this_week.about: Network sci-fi mystery (originally NBC, 2021–2024) — a massive sinkhole opens in Los Angeles, pulling people and buildings into a prehistoric land. Full four-season run dropped on Netflix on May 1 as a binge package.
new_this_week.why: Sci-fi premise + world building + complete run (no future-season anxiety) checks three of your reward signals. Network-pacing means commercial-break beats — try one episode to see if the writing carries it past 'try.'

new_this_week.title: Apex
new_this_week.about: Charlize Theron plays Sasha, an experienced climber grieving the loss of her partner; alone in the Australian wilderness, what begins as endurance becomes a cat-and-mouse hunt with a methodical predator (Taron Egerton). Directed by Baltasar Kormákur. Eric Bana co-stars.
new_this_week.why: Pure survival thriller — strong premise but no off-beat humor or sci-fi/supernatural angle to push it past 'try.' Good if you specifically want a tense one-night watch.

new_this_week.title: Devil May Cry S2
new_this_week.date: May 12 — all 8 eps drop at once
new_this_week.about: Adi Shankar adult-animation series adapted from Capcom's action-RPG franchise, Studio Mir animating (The Legend of Korra, Voltron). S2 centers on the Dante–Vergil rivalry with a darker, more personal arc. 8 episodes binge-drop May 12. Returning cast: Johnny Yong Bosch (Dante), Robbie Daymond (Vergil), Scout Taylor-Compton (Lady).
new_this_week.why: Adult animation + supernatural + 30-min episodes triple-stacks your signals — same shelf as Solar Opposites and Castlevania. Studio Mir's craft is reliable, and S1 set up the Dante–Vergil collision the season is finally paying off. Pinned for the week of May 11+.

new_this_week.title: Widow's Bay
new_this_week.date: Apr 28 — airing weekly (Ep 3 drops Wed May 7)
new_this_week.about: Matthew Rhys-led comedy-horror, Katie Dippold creator. 100% RT (34 reviews) on debut. Small coastal town, supernatural undercurrents, off-beat tone.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. 100% RT, off-beat horror-comedy, supernatural, ensemble — quadruple-stacks your reward signals. (Also today's hero pick — see top.)

new_this_week.title: The Boys S5 (Final)
new_this_week.about: Final season, eight episodes, weekly Wednesdays through May 20. 95% RT through 55 reviews. Wraps up Homelander vs. Butcher. Garth Ennis source material; ensemble dark comedy with the show's usual escalation.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. Last-season urgency + dark satire + plot escalation aligns with your reward signals. Always gross-out adjacent — pace yourself if that's a sticking point.

new_this_week.title: Kevin
new_this_week.about: Aubrey Plaza and Joe Wengert's animated series. Jason Schwartzman voices Kevin, a housecat who decides to try life without people; Plaza voices Dana, one of the humans he leaves behind. All 8 episodes dropped at once. Star-studded guest cast.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. Adult animation + off-beat humor + 30-min episodes triple-stacks your signals — same pocket as Solar Opposites and Rick and Morty. Plaza's deadpan comedy DNA fits your dark-humor reward pattern.

new_this_week.title: The House of the Spirits
new_this_week.about: Eight-part adaptation of Isabel Allende's 1982 novel. Multi-generational saga of the Trueba family in Chile, blending political turmoil with magical realism. First three episodes premiered Apr 29; finale May 13. 80% RT. Spanish-language with Latin American/Spanish cast.
new_this_week.why: Book adaptation + supernatural/magical-realism elements hit positive signals; Spanish-language watch is also a Spanish-tutor side-benefit. Multi-generational drama is heavier than your typical pick — try the first episode.

new_this_week.title: Tom Clancy's Jack Ryan: Ghost War
new_this_week.about: Feature film continuation of the Prime Video series. John Krasinski returns as Jack Ryan, with Wendell Pierce and Michael Kelly back from the show; Sienna Miller joins. Ryan is reluctantly thrust back into espionage when a covert mission unravels a deadly conspiracy and a rogue black-ops unit. 105 min, releases globally May 20.
new_this_week.why: Action-thriller lane — you 4⭐'d Mission: Impossible: The Final Reckoning so 'entertaining + hi-tech' espionage works. No supernatural/sci-fi anchor and no off-beat humor, so it stays at 'try.' One-night watch.

new_this_week.title: Spider-Noir
new_this_week.about: Nicolas Cage stars as a 1930s private detective Spider-Man. Live-action take on the Spider-Verse Spider-Noir character. Eight episodes from Amazon MGM. Drops May 27. Rotten Tomatoes ranks it #1 most-anticipated TV show for May 2026.
new_this_week.why: Stylized noir setting + Cage's full-commit acting could play to the off-beat signal. No supernatural/sci-fi anchor — flag for end of May.

new_this_week.title: The Boroughs
new_this_week.date: May 21 — all 8 episodes drop at once
new_this_week.about: Sci-fi/supernatural series from Duffer Brothers (Stranger Things) as EPs; Jeffrey Addiss and Will Matthews showrun. Set in a New Mexico retirement community where senior citizens must stop an otherworldly threat from stealing the one thing they don't have: time. Cast: Bill Pullman, Alfre Woodard, Alfred Molina, Geena Davis. Eight episodes binge-drop.
new_this_week.why: Supernatural + world building + ensemble cast triple-stacks your signals; Duffer Bros pedigree means a real plot-twist machine. Older-cast 'Stranger Things for seniors' framing is the kind of off-beat hook you reward.

new_this_week.title: Witch Hat Atelier
new_this_week.about: Long-awaited adaptation of Kamome Shirahama's manga. Coco, a young girl who dreams of becoming a witch, gets her chance after a chance encounter with a traveling magician. Heavy on world building and visual craft.
new_this_week.why: Fantasy anime with strong world building hits your sweet spot. Coming-of-age tone is lighter than your usual but the magic-system rigor scratches the same itch as Foundation/Sandman.

new_this_week.title: Dorohedoro S2
new_this_week.about: Long-delayed S2 of the cult-favorite manga adaptation. Caiman, a man with a reptile head and amnesia, hunts the sorcerer who cursed him. Vibe: gruesome but absurdly funny, with deep world building.
new_this_week.why: Dark humor + supernatural + off-beat — three of your strongest signals stacked. Body-horror visuals are gnarly but they're load-bearing for the comedy. Worth catching up on S1 if you didn't.

new_this_week.title: Chainsaw Man — The Movie: Reze Arc
new_this_week.about: First feature-length film in MAPPA's Chainsaw Man series. Adapts manga chapters 39–52 covering the entire Reze Arc — Denji's romance with a barista who is not what she seems. Premiered theatrically in Japan in Sept 2025; landed on Crunchyroll Apr 30 with both subbed and dubbed versions as part of Crunchyroll's Ani-May celebration.
new_this_week.why: Dark humor + supernatural + plot-twist machinery + MAPPA's animation craft — Chainsaw Man's tone is Demon-Slayer-adjacent with sharper teeth. Reze Arc is widely considered the best self-contained Chainsaw Man story; works as a standalone if you haven't watched the TV series.

new_this_week.title: Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed
new_this_week.date: May 20 — premieres with 2 eps, weekly through Jul 15
new_this_week.about: Darkly comedic thriller from creator David J. Rosen. Emmy winner Tatiana Maslany plays Paula, a newly divorced mom who falls down a dangerous rabbit hole of blackmail, murder, and youth soccer. 10 episodes, half-hour, premieres with two eps May 20 then weekly Wednesdays through July 15.
new_this_week.why: Dark comedy-thriller + 30-min episodes + Maslany's Orphan Black ensemble pedigree triple-stacks your reward signals. Premieres mid-month — flag now so it's on your radar when CDMX trip wraps.

new_this_week.title: Ladies First
new_this_week.about: Sacha Baron Cohen and Rosamund Pike face off in a gender-swap satire — high-powered ad exec Damien Sachs wakes up in a parallel world where women hold all the power, going head-to-head with the underestimated Alex Fox (Pike) for the top job. Directed by Thea Sharrock; screenplay by Natalie Krinsky, Cinco Paul, Katie Silberman.
new_this_week.why: Alt-reality premise + satirical comedy + Baron Cohen's commit — flirts with your off-beat sweet spot. Satire is the genre lane Solar Opposites lives in. No supernatural/sci-fi anchor though, so it stays at 'try.' Good Friday-night one-and-done.

critics.date: May 4 — now streaming, all 4 eps available
critics.about: Four-episode BBC/Netflix miniseries from Jack Thorne adapting Golding's novel. THR: 'very close to a definitive adaptation.' Critics 92% / audience 57%.
critics.why: Highest-RT new drop on a service you have this week. Book adaptation lands; tonal darkness is the watch-out — see new this week for the full why.

critics.title: Widow's Bay
critics.about: Matthew Rhys-led comedy-horror, Katie Dippold creator. 100% RT (34 reviews) on debut.
critics.why: Critic darling that also nails your taste profile — that's why it's today's hero pick.

critics.title: Jo Nesbø's Detective Hole
critics.about: Nine-episode Norwegian crime series adapting Jo Nesbø's fifth Harry Hole novel, The Devil's Star. Tobias Santelmann plays the brooding lead detective; Joel Kinnaman is his colleague. Currently a global Netflix top-10 hit. 91% RT — RT consensus calls it 'twisty, stylish, and at times gloriously grim.'
critics.why: Nordic noir with plot twists, ensemble acting, and brooding-detective DNA — directly adjacent to the Slow Horses lane you 4⭐'d. The 9-episode runtime gets one critic ding (a tighter 5–6 would be sharper) but the writing carries it. Subs needed; you're open to that.
